content.text:
I submitted index 14 (Mg 0.80 / Mn 0.20) as the best composition. At 7×10⁻⁸ A it had the highest photocurrent of the three samples I could measure, but that signal is very small.

All three merit measurements are used:

| Index | Composition | Why I chose it | Photocurrent |
|---|---|---|---|
| 12 | Mg 0.33 / Mn 0.67 | Matches the MgMn2O4 spinel, which the models predicted is stable and absorbs 3.22 eV light (gap 2.87 eV) | 0 |
| 14 | Mg 0.80 / Mn 0.20 | Most Mg-rich sample; Mg3MnO4 is predicted to absorb (gap 2.24 eV) | 7×10⁻⁸ A |
| 2 | Mg 0.10 / Mn 0.90 | Checked the untested Mn-rich end; its phases have small gaps (about 1 eV) | 1×10⁻⁸ A |

- **The spinel prediction was wrong:** index 12, which the models favoured most, gave nothing.
- **Coverage is thin:** with only three measurements, the Mg-rich side (Mg 0.57–0.78) is untested. Index 14 was the most Mg-rich sample, so I can't tell whether it's a real peak or just the end of the range.
- **No XRD used:** I didn't use any of the 5 XRD measurements, so the phases actually present in these samples weren't checked.
